findings.title: Duplicate definition of OptimizedImage.downsize silently replaces the width/height version
findings.body: The file now defines self.downsize twice: at line 145 as downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}) and again at line 149 as downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}). In Ruby the last definition wins, so the width/height version at line 145 is dead code, and any existing caller (including specs) that invokes OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, width, height) will now raise ArgumentError (wrong number of arguments, 5 for 3..4) at runtime. Keep a single signature: either delete the width/height variant, or have it build the dimensions string and delegate to the new one.

findings.title: Downsize loop reads size from a stale file handle and ignores downsize failures
findings.body: The loop condition `while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` uses Tempfile#size, which is fstat() on the already-open file handle. OptimizedImage.downsize -> convert_with runs ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which — when it improves the image (the common case) — replaces the file at tempfile.path by moving a newly written file over it, i.e. a new inode. The open handle keeps pointing at the old, unlinked inode, so tempfile.size stays frozen at the size captured after the first convert and never reflects further reductions. Consequences: (1) an image that needs more than one pass to get under the limit is downsized all 5 times — shrunk to 0.8^5 ≈ 33% of its dimensions and lossily recompressed/optimized five times, degrading quality and burning CPU; (2) the same stale tempfile.size is passed to Upload.create_for on line 72, so an image that was actually reduced below the limit can be stored with, and validated against, its old larger filesize and still be rejected. The loop also ignores OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failing convert is retried identically five times. Check File.size(tempfile.path), pass that value to create_for, and break out of the loop when downsize returns false.

findings.title: Client-side upload size check hardcodes 10 MB and ignores max_image_size_kb / max_attachment_size_kb
findings.body: validateUploadedFile used to check file size against Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']; it now uses a hardcoded 10 * 1024 for every upload type. This breaks the attachment path: a forum with max_attachment_size_kb set above 10 MB (e.g. to allow zips or videos) now has legitimate uploads rejected in the browser, and a forum with a lower attachment limit lets oversized files through only to fail on the server after the upload. For images it also ignores the configured limit in both directions — sites that raised max_image_size_kb above 10 MB still block larger images client-side — and the file_too_large message always reports 10 MB regardless of the actual setting. The per-type site settings should remain the source of truth, with any extra headroom for server-side downsizing applied only to type 'image'.

findings.title: API URL-download size cap hardcoded to 10 MB instead of max_image_size_kb
findings.body: FileHelper.download for URL-based API uploads is now called with 10.megabytes rather than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. On sites where the admin raised the image size limit above 10 MB, downloads that used to succeed now exceed the hardcoded cap; FileHelper.download raises, the rescue sets tempfile to nil, and the code then hits the pre-existing nil-tempfile path (tempfile.size at line 72 raises NoMethodError), turning a previously valid upload into a 500. The cap should stay tied to the site setting (or a single shared constant) instead of a magic number that can drift from configuration.

findings.title: 413 error message now always claims the upload limit is 10 MB
findings.body: The 413 (entity too large) handler in displayErrorForUpload used to report Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb in the file_too_large message; it now hardcodes 10 * 1024. Whenever the site's configured limit, or the web server's actual body-size limit that produced the 413, differs from 10 MB, the user is shown the wrong maximum size. The message should use the site setting or the real configured limit.

findings.title: No tests for the auto-downsize upload path
findings.body: This PR adds a server-side resize loop to UploadsController#create_upload and changes OptimizedImage.downsize's signature, but no specs were added or updated (only these three files changed). There is no coverage for: an oversized image being downsized below max_image_size_kb and accepted, termination when the image cannot be reduced enough, the animated-GIF branch, or the new downsize signature. Given the subtleties involved (the downsize tool replacing the file vs. the open tempfile handle, and the duplicate method definition in optimized_image.rb), controller and model specs should be added before merging.
